subject: Pricing & commitment path: trial -> commit options and $/1M target
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan@horizonai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pricing & commitment path: trial -> commit options and $/1M target

Hi Ethan / Samira —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can align internally and get you a clean offer: 

Summary of what you told us
- Current proof-of-concept: 2 ML engineers, 1 product owner running experimental chat and embedding flows.
- Expected ramp over 6 months: ~40M tokens/mo -> 150M tokens/mo at scale (peak).
- Targeting an effective rate in the ballpark of $700–$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on latency/throughput SLAs.
- Budget signal: $40k–$60k/month if unit economics align.

What you asked for
- An early-stage startup credit to offset initial POC spend.
- A committed-use option (12 or 24 months) with larger discounts and predictable unit rate.
- Quick procurement path — need a simple SOW and a pricing sheet to show finance.

Options we can put on the table (attached as scenarios):
1) Trial + Top-up credits: 90-day trial with $10k accelerator credit applied to usage, followed by pay-as-you-go at our standard startup tier.
2) 12-month commit: 12mo committed spend with ~30% off list for the committed volume band (targeting $900/1M at 100M tokens/mo equivalent) + 30k onboarding credit spread over first 3 months.
3) 24-month commit: 24mo with deeper unit discount (~40% off) and an introductory invoice credit (one-time $25k) to support runway; includes a mid-term volume rebaselining clause.

Open items we need from you to firm an offer
- Confirm the expected monthly token profile (first 3 months, months 4–6, steady-state).
- Any procurement constraints (PO vs. SOW, billing contact).
- Whether Horizon qualifies for our seed/accelerator enhanced credit (company stage and cap table note).

Immediate next steps
- I attached a pricing scenarios PDF + a one-page mutual action plan. Ben/Marissa — can you review the 12mo/24mo numbers and confirm if legal/proc can accept the proposed credit structure?
- Ethan/Samira — if you can share a 3-month token ramp by EOD Friday we’ll produce a firm pricing quote and a draft SOW for procurement.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-pricing-scenarios-v3.pdf (1 page summary)
Attachment: mutual-action-plan-horizon.xlsx (stub)

From: Ethan Cole <ethan@horizonai.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Voss <samira@horizonai.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & commitment path: trial -> commit options and $/1M target

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear recap. Helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Ramp profile (provisional): month 1: 15M tokens, month 2: 45M, month 3: 90M, month 4–6: 120–150M steady.
2) Budget: finance would be comfortable with ~$50k/month if we can get to <= $850/1M at steady state.
3) Credits: the $10k accelerator credit is useful — can that be frontloaded as a billing credit on month 1?
4) Procurement: we use a standard PO workflow; legal will need a simple SOW.

Given runway constraints, we’d strongly prefer a 12mo commit with a true unit-rate guarantee vs. a % discount on list. If you can show a fixed $/1M for a 12mo band (plus the accelerator credit), we can move quickly.

Can you put a sample 12mo table in $/1M terms (best / expected / stretch)? That will let finance model it into the cap table plan.

—Ethan
Principal Product Manager, Horizon AI

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan@horizonai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & commitment path: trial -> commit options and $/1M target

Ethan —

Appreciate the ramp detail — that helps a lot. Attached I’ve uploaded a short table that translates the scenario into explicit $/1M amounts (see redwood-pricing-scenarios-v3.pdf). Quick preview: 

- Trial + $10k credit: standard startup tier -> effective ~ $1,050/1M for early months (low volume).
- 12mo commit (target band 100M tokens/mo): guaranteed $850/1M at 100M equivalent, with a 3-month credit amortization ($30k onboarding credit) — effective blended rate for year1 closer to $760/1M if you hit the ramp.
- 24mo commit (same band): guaranteed $700/1M with the one-time $25k invoice credit — favorable if you expect steady growth beyond 18 months.

Ben / Marissa — can you confirm legal/proc and whether we can offer the $30k onboarding credit amortized over 3 months for the 12mo? Also, are the 12mo/24mo offers constrained by any CFO-level approval thresholds (i.e., > $500k ARR commit)?

If those are green, Ethan — I’ll draft a one-page SOW + pricing appendix you can send to procurement. We can lock the DocuSign link and PO flow once legal gives the thumbs up.

Best,
Naomi

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-19T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & commitment path: trial -> commit options and $/1M target

Naomi / Marissa — quick internal reply: 

Legal/proc reviewed the MOP and the onboarding credit structure — procurement is ok with amortized credits as long as the SOW explicitly lays out credit schedule and the PO references the pricing appendix. CFO sign-off: any commitment > $600k ARR equivalent requires REVOPS approval but we can approve up to $600k at AE/Manager level.

We can offer the following firm options to present to Horizon: 
A) 12mo commit (band = 100M tokens/mo equivalent): fixed $850/1M guaranteed. $30k onboarding credit amortized over first 3 invoices. No additional CFO approval needed if annual bill <= $600k.
B) 24mo commit (band = 100M tokens/mo equivalent): fixed $720/1M guaranteed. One-time invoice credit $25k. Requires VP RevOps approval for multi-year.
C) Trial + $10k accelerator credit: immediate billing credit, then standard startup tier rates.

Naomi — you can present option A as the near-term close path (matches their finance target). If Ethan confirms the ramp, draft the SOW and I’ll prep the pricing appendix and route for stamp.

Ben
Director, Growth — Redwood Inference
